quotes.name: Philly Rodriguez
quotes.quote: Yeah, we lost three. It wasn't layoffs — it was attrition, people moving on. Two of them were dealers who got offers down in San Jose, and one was a security guy who went back to school. I can't give you their names, that's not my place. But I'll tell you this: nobody who stayed got a raise, and nobody got a cut either. Hours are the same, pay's the same. The floor's just a little thinner now, so we're all covering a bit more. The casino's not hurting — it's just not growing. And that's the thing about this town right now: the places around us in Baylight and Jack London are adding a job here and there, and we're the ones giving one up. I don't know what that says about who gains from the casino, but I know what it feels like to walk the floor with three fewer familiar faces.

quotes.name: Manfred Owens
quotes.quote: Yeah, I saw the numbers on the board — three people gone from the casino this cycle. I can't tell you exactly who they were, not by name, because I don't have that list in front of me. But I can tell you what it feels like from my seat near the back. The floor's a little thinner at the tables on weeknights, and the shifts have been stretched. Philly's been covering more of the floor himself, and Gregory's been doing double duty on the stuff nobody talks about. I've picked up a couple extra hours myself, just to keep the ledger straight. The firms around us in Baylight and Jack London each added a spot, but that doesn't put food on the table for the folks who got let go here. It's a strange thing — the neighborhood feels like it's moving forward, and we're just holding the line.
